criteria.criterion: The root cause is named in the change description and CHANGELOG.md: nothing makes the producer measure a new or tightened refusal rule against past accepted readings while it works. The replay (`replay_stage` in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs) runs once after the producer finishes, as a verification hold. Checked by reading the diff.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] > Added reads: "Root cause: nothing made the producer measure a new or tightened refusal rule against past accepted readings while it worked. The replay (`replay_stage`) ran once, after the producer finished, as a hold at verification". The same statement is in the doc comments on `LoopReplay`, `Athena::loop_replay` and `producer_loop`, and in docs/architecture.md. The fix is in `producer_loop` (producer.rs:276-302), which calls `loop_replay` after each parsed report. It is not tied to any single rule.

They use a fake candidate checker that newly refuses more than the limit of a corpus of recorded accepted readings. They assert that the producer is sent back, that its brief names the newly refused job ids and the measured percent, and that the loop ends once the share is under the limit. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

It drives a whole job through `Athena::go`, with `seed_accepted_jobs(10, 3)` as the history and a candidate checker installed through the replay seam that refuses the marked readings only until the producer's second run. It asserts: two producer prompts, and only the second contains `## Sent back`; the second names the three seeded job ids, `30%` and `limit 10%`; the in-loop lines show 3 of 10 and then 0 of 10, both before the checks; the job ends Landed; replay.json has 0 newly refused. On the base tree there is no send-back for the replay and no in-loop line, so those assertions would fail. Athena's revert run (fails-without-2) exited 101, but because the new functions do not exist and the test did not compile. The full suite passed per Athena's CI record (`cargo test --locked`).

findings.summary: A file outside the expected deliverables changed: crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs
findings.evidence: The only change makes `slot_limit_bytes` `pub(super)` so that `loop_replay` can size the build slot's target directory. It is small and needed by the mechanism, but checks.rs is not on the expected deliverables list or among the planned files.

findings.summary: The producer brief writes the replay limit as literal text instead of deriving it from the constants
findings.evidence: The section says "more than 10% of them ... plus 5 points" as fixed text. The real limit comes from `REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT` and `REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS` in athena-core. If either constant changes, the brief will state the wrong limit. The limit in the send-back itself is computed, so the producer is still told the correct limit when it is sent back.

findings.summary: For criterion 2, the revert run showed only that the tests do not compile without the change, not that a behavior assertion fails
findings.evidence: Athena's fails-without-2 run exited 101 because `send_back_text_with_replay` and `touches_reading_rules` were not found. Reading the tests, their behavior assertions (two prompts, `## Sent back` with the ids and percent, the in-loop lines, Landed) could not pass on the base tree, so this is a weakness of the demonstration, not of the tests.

summary: The change fixes the cause where it starts. Before, the replay of past accepted readings ran only once, after the producer had finished (`replay_stage`, the hold at verification). Now `producer_loop` calls a new `Athena::loop_replay` after each report whose changes touch `crates/` or the Cargo files. It reuses the existing replay functions (`replay_cases`, `replay`, `replay_checkers`) and the same limit, now in `replay_limit_percent`: 10%, or the declared share plus 5. It takes a build slot for its two builds. When the share is over the limit, the producer is sent back inside the existing retry budget, with the newly refused job ids, the measured percent and the limit. A replay that cannot run prints `replay     in the loop: no replay: <reason>` and is never a pass. The hold at verification stays as the backstop and reuses the loop's result only for the same base, tree and readings. The CHANGELOG, docs/architecture.md and the doc comments name the root cause. I ran all 12 new athena-core tests and the new athena-context brief test, and all passed. They cover the send-back with ids and share, the loop ending under the limit, exactly 10% passing and 20% being sent back, the declared share plus 5, an unrunnable replay, an empty history, a docs-only change, a held build slot, and the hold reusing the loop's result. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's CI record. I found three minor issues and no blocker or major one: (1) crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs changed although it is not on the deliverables list; (2) the producer brief writes the limit as the literal text "10%" and "plus 5 points" instead of deriving it from the constants; (3) Athena's revert run for criterion 2 failed only because the tests would not compile, not on a behavior assertion.
